title: Pad see ew

items: 12 oz fresh wide rice noodles (or 6 oz dried wide rice noodles, soaked as the package says)
8 oz boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast, sliced ¼ inch thick
3 cups broccoli florets in bite-size pieces, or 1 bunch Chinese broccoli (stems cut into 1-inch pieces, leaves kept separate)

steps: Separate the noodles into single strands. If they're stiff from the fridge, microwave them 30–60 sec, until they pull apart without tearing.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, dark soy, sugar and 1 Tbsp water in the small bowl until the sugar dissolves.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in the wok over high heat until it shimmers. Add the chicken in one layer and cook 2 min without moving it. Add the garlic and stir-fry 1–2 min more, until the chicken is no longer pink and reads 165°F.
Add the broccoli (stems first if using Chinese broccoli) and 2 Tbsp water. Stir-fry 2 min, until bright green and crisp-tender. Add any Chinese broccoli leaves for the last 30 sec.
Push everything to one side. Add 1 Tbsp oil to the empty side, crack in the eggs and scramble 30–60 sec, until just set.

Add the last 1 Tbsp oil, the noodles and the sauce. Toss gently to coat. Then spread them out and let them sit undisturbed 30 sec at a time, tossing between, for 2–3 min total, until they have charred spots.
Toss everything together and serve right away.
tips: Don't double it in one pan. Cook 2 batches, or the noodles steam and break instead of charring.
No dark soy sauce? Use 1 extra tsp soy sauce plus 1 tsp molasses or brown sugar.
Try a pinch of chili flakes and a splash of rice vinegar at the table, the way Thai restaurants serve it.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Rice noodles harden when cold, so reheat in a skillet over medium heat with 1–2 Tbsp water, covered for 1 min, or microwave covered with a damp paper towel. Doesn't freeze well.
